chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Abi Sa'id, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abd Allah and Abi Ja'far, peace be upon them.

They, peace be upon them, said: “The salat is not to be repeated because of blood that one did not see, except the blood of menstruation, for indeed its small amount and its large amount on the garment are the same, whether one saw it or did not see it.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing on which impurity may be present
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.دَمٍ: blood as a substance affecting ritual purity rulings
key_terms.دَمَ الْحَيْضِ: menstrual blood, treated as an exception in this ruling
key_terms.لَا تُعَادُ: is not to be repeated; indicates non-obligation of repeating the prayer

ai.seo_question: Must salat be repeated if blood is later found on one's garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding blood on clothing during salat. It states that salat is not repeated due to blood that was unnoticed, except menstrual blood, whose small and large amounts are treated equally on a garment whether seen or unseen.
